note: Closed list of advice claim types for the optional 'check the AI's advice' add-on (handoff 106). Claude only splits pasted advice into claims and picks one claim_type per claim. Code runs the data check, picks the verdict and confidence from this table, and fills the explanation template. Written 2026-11-06. Thresholds and confidences are our own illustrative choices.

absence_evidence_ids.FILE-ACCOUNTS: The list of accounts on the file (used to show something is NOT on the file, e.g. a student loan)
absence_evidence_ids.FILE-ASSOC: The financial associations list on the file (empty for Jordan)

claim_types.for_claude: Advice to make several credit applications, apply to more lenders, or apply again soon.
claim_types.data_check: Count hard searches in the last 90 days (rule R-SRCH).

outcomes.when: 1 or more hard searches in the last 90 days
outcomes.template: You already have {hard_90d} hard searches in the last 90 days, on {search_dates}. Each application adds another, and Experian suggests at most one every three months. A soft-search eligibility check does not show to lenders.

outcomes.when: no hard searches in the last 90 days
outcomes.template: Each application adds a hard search, and Experian suggests at most one every three months. Apply to one lender at a time, after a soft-search eligibility check.

claim_types.evidence: Each hard search in the last 90 days, plus sources S-EXP-REFUSED and S-CO-MYTHS.

claim_types.for_claude: A claim about how long late or missed payments stay on a credit file, or that one has already gone.
claim_types.data_check: Find late or missed payment entries (status 1 or worse). Drop-off date = recorded date plus 6 years.

outcomes.when: a late entry exists and the claim says it is gone or lasts under 6 years
outcomes.template: Your file still shows the late payment recorded on {late_recorded}. Experian says a late payment stays for six years, so it drops off on {late_drop}.

outcomes.when: no late entry on the file
outcomes.template: Your file has no late payments, so this does not apply to you.

claim_types.evidence: The late entry, plus source S-EXP-LATE.

claim_types.for_claude: Advice to register to vote or join the electoral roll.
claim_types.data_check: Rule R-ROLL, plus the first rent or deposit payment to the current landlord.

outcomes.template: Your rent has gone to {landlord} since {first_rent_date}, but the electoral roll on your file is only at your previous address. Registering by {register_by} should show on your file from {roll_clears_on}.
Good advice in general, and you are already on the electoral roll at your current address.

claim_types.evidence: The first rent payment to the current landlord, ER entries, the current address, plus sources S-EXP-ROLL and S-EXP-REFUSED.

claim_types.for_claude: Advice to pay a card down before its statement date so a lower balance is reported.
claim_types.data_check: Find a revolving account with a statement_day and its latest reported entry.

outcomes.when: a revolving account with a statement day exists
outcomes.template: Your {card_lender} statement date is the {statement_day}th, and your file shows statement balances, for example £{latest_balance} on {latest_statement_date}. Paying before {next_statement_date} lowers the next one. Reporting dates vary by lender, and Experian says reports can take around 4 to 8 weeks to update.

claim_types.evidence: The card account and its latest reported entry, plus source S-EXP-UTIL.
claim_types.caveat: Confidence is 0.7 because we did not verify that every lender reports the statement balance. In our synthetic file the reported balance is the statement balance by construction.

claim_types.for_claude: A claim that a student loan is hurting a credit application or credit score.
claim_types.data_check: Look for an account of type student_loan on the file.

outcomes.when: no student loan on the file
outcomes.template: There is no student loan on your file, and Capital One UK says a student loan does not directly affect your credit score. Your file shows {n_fail} other reasons instead: {fail_names}.

claim_types.caveat: 0.85, not higher, because a lender's own affordability check may still look at student loan deductions from pay. We do not see that.

claim_types.for_claude: A claim that previous occupants, neighbours or the address itself affect your credit.
claim_types.data_check: Look at financial_associations on the file.

outcomes.template: Your file shows no financial associations, and Capital One UK says previous occupants of your home cannot affect your credit score.

claim_types.for_claude: Advice to take a payday loan or other short-term high-cost loan.
claim_types.data_check: Count hard searches in the last 90 days (a new loan application adds one).

outcomes.template: Experian says a payday loan usually does not damage your score if repaid on time, but advises avoiding one before an important credit application. Applying would also add a hard search to the {hard_90d} you already have in the last 90 days.

claim_types.evidence: Each hard search in the last 90 days, plus sources S-EXP-PAYDAY and S-EXP-SEARCH.

claim_types.for_claude: Advice to close a credit card or have fewer cards to improve your chances.
claim_types.data_check: Count revolving accounts and their limits.

outcomes.when: the card is the only revolving account
outcomes.template: Your {card_lender} is your only card and holds your whole £{limit} limit. Closing it removes that limit, and lenders look at how much of your available credit you use. Paying it down helps more.

claim_types.evidence: The card account, plus source S-EXP-LIMITS.

claim_types.for_claude: Anything else, including market predictions, interest rate forecasts or general opinions.

outcomes.template: We cannot check this against your file or transactions. Treat it as unverified.

quotes: Most eligibility check tools use a soft search, which does not affect your score and cannot be seen by lenders.
No, your student loan does not directly impact your credit score positively or negatively.
The financial history of a person is not attached to their address, and that means that the previous occupants of your house also cannot affect your credit score.
Each hard check is recorded on your report, so any company searching it will be able to see that you’ve applied for credit.
